title: audit_entries.resource_id UUID/TEXT saga: original dispatch-skip defect RESOLVED; follow-on defect is 6+ test files still casting the (now-TEXT) resource_id bind param to ::uuid
summary: Discovered while verifying the ISS-0093 fix (removal of the stale GBL-081 DISABLE TRIGGER ALL shim in tests/integration/helpers.zig): once the audit triggers on the six business tables were re-enabled for real, tenant_default.audit_entries.resource_id was found to still be UUID-typed (not TEXT), and tenant_default's copies of bpm_audit_chain_canonical_payload/bpm_audit_compute_chain_hash/bpm_audit_on_mutation still declared/used UUID-typed resource_id parameters/variables -- exactly the type mismatch GBL-082 was written to fix. Root cause: src/db/migrations.zig Migrations.runForSchema() (lines ~196-207) unconditionally skips every 'GBL-'-prefixed migration filename when schema_name != 'public', with a comment justifying this because most GBL-* migrations perform DDL on public-only tables (tenant_schemas, onboarding_registry, tnt05_progress, etc.). However GBL-081_iss103_audit_resource_id_text.sql and GBL-082_fix_audit_chain_resource_id_text.sql are NOT public-only -- both are written as per-schema migrations (GBL-081 explicitly loops via `current_schema()` and `format('ALTER TABLE %I...', v_schema)`; GBL-082 issues unqualified CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION statements that land in whichever schema is first on search_path) and operate on audit_entries, a table that exists independently in every tenant schema (see migrations/020_obs03_audit_entries.sql, applied per-schema). Because runForSchema() skips them purely by filename prefix regardless of what they actually touch, tenant_default (and by the same code path, every real per-tenant schema created via provisionTenantSchema()) never receives the resource_id UUID->TEXT conversion or the corrected audit-chain function signatures. The type mismatch is normally invisible because ISS-0093's now-removed shim disabled the audit trigger entirely, so the mismatched INSERT never ran; with that shim removed, tenant_default's audit trigger fires with a still-UUID resource_id parameter chain, causing intermittent test failures (TC-ISS-103-INT-01: pg_typeof(resource_id) is 'uuid' not 'text') that appear/disappear depending on migration/test run order and which test binary happens to run tenant schema provisioning first in a given process invocation. This is a production-impacting defect, not just a test artifact: any real tenant schema provisioned via provisionTenantSchema() (src/db/provisioning.zig, which itself calls runForSchema()) will have the same permanently-unconverted resource_id column and audit-chain function signatures as tenant_default currently does in the test database.

root_cause.details: src/db/migrations.zig Migrations.runForSchema(), lines 196-207: `if (!std.mem.eql(u8, schema_name, "public") and std.mem.startsWith(u8, filename, "GBL-")) { continue; }` -- this treats the 'GBL-' filename prefix as a proxy for 'is this migration global/public-only', which holds for most GBL-* files (confirmed by inspection: GBL-073 through GBL-080, GBL-083 through GBL-085, GBL-097 through GBL-101 all reference public-only tables like tenant_schemas/onboarding_registry/tnt05_progress/rate_limit_buckets/state_snapshots) but does NOT hold for GBL-081 and GBL-082, which are the only two GBL-prefixed migrations that operate on a table (audit_entries) that is legitimately per-tenant-schema. Neither GBL-081 nor GBL-082 references any table confirmed to be global-only (grepped for public.tenant_schemas, public.onboarding_registry, public.tnt05_progress in both files -- zero matches). GBL-081 was in fact explicitly designed to be schema-generic (uses current_schema()/format(%I, v_schema) throughout) but the skip-by-prefix rule in runForSchema() prevents it from ever running against any schema except 'public', defeating that design intent for every tenant schema that has ever existed or will ever be provisioned.

files_to_change: (ORIGINAL, RESOLVED) src/db/migrations.zig -- runForSchema()'s GBL-skip rule; superseded by the explicit `-- scope:` header mechanism now in place (see migrationScope() and SCOPE_PUBLIC_HEADER).

(CURRENT, OPEN) tests/integration/ext02_webhook_dispatch_test.zig, obs03_audit_log_test.zig, obs05_dlq_test.zig, adp02_tenant_scope_test.zig, adp06_pipeline_run_correlation_test.zig, oidc09_jit_provisioning_test.zig -- remove the `::uuid` cast from `resource_id = $N::uuid` (grep -rn "resource_id = \$[0-9]::uuid" tests/integration/ to enumerate every call site precisely before fixing, some files have multiple occurrences).
resolution: ORIGINAL PREMISE RESOLVED (confirmed 2026-08-08 during ISS-0184/GH-517 diagnosis): live inspection of the current test database shows tenant_default.audit_entries.resource_id is now genuinely TEXT (`\d+ tenant_default.audit_entries` -> resource_id | text | ... | not null), not UUID. The runForSchema() GBL-skip dispatch defect this issue describes has evidently been fixed by later work (migrations.zig now supports an explicit `-- scope:` header per migrationScope(), separate from filename-prefix inference -- see migration 1107_fix_audit_chain_text_resource_id.sql's own `-- scope:` usage), so the specific symptom recorded here (resource_id staying UUID-typed in tenant schemas) no longer reproduces. HOWEVER: fixing the column type surfaced a follow-on, opposite-direction defect that is NOT yet fixed -- at least 6 test files (ext02_webhook_dispatch_test.zig, obs03_audit_log_test.zig, obs05_dlq_test.zig, adp02_tenant_scope_test.zig, adp06_pipeline_run_correlation_test.zig, oidc09_jit_provisioning_test.zig, plus cascading failures in xc02/xc06/exp201_202/exp401_402/exp601/repository_test/sim01_04) still bind their query parameter as `resource_id = $N::uuid` against the now-TEXT column, producing PostgreSQL C42883 'operator does not exist: text = uuid' (reproduced directly via a prepared statement against tenant_default). This is call-site drift that was never updated when the column type fix landed, not a recurrence of the original dispatch bug. Tracked as a new occurrence below rather than a new issue number, since it is the same resource_id-type story continuing. See docs/issue-reports/ISS-0184-diagnosis.yaml cluster C1 for the full failing-test list and reproduction.

occurrences.context: After removing the stale GBL-081 DISABLE TRIGGER ALL shim from tests/integration/helpers.zig::applyCompatibilityShims() per the ISS-0093 validated design, re-running zig build test-integration-iss103 surfaced 4/4 test failures instead of the design's predicted 3/4-then-4/4. Root-caused to tenant_default.audit_entries.resource_id still being UUID-typed (pg_typeof(resource_id) returned 'uuid' not 'text') and tenant_default's copies of bpm_audit_chain_canonical_payload/bpm_audit_compute_chain_hash/bpm_audit_on_mutation still using UUID-typed resource_id, despite migrations/GBL-082_fix_audit_chain_resource_id_text.sql being recorded as applied for schema_name='public' in public.schema_migrations. Confirmed via direct psql inspection against the running r-co-db_test-1 container (docker exec) and by reading src/db/migrations.zig's runForSchema() GBL-skip logic (lines 196-207): GBL-081/082 are permanently skipped for schema_name != 'public', so tenant_default never received either migration's effect despite audit_entries being a per-tenant table. Manually applied both migration files' SQL bodies with search_path set to tenant_default to unblock ISS-0093's own acceptance-criteria verification (test-integration-iss103 confirmed passing 4/4 in isolation after the manual fix), but confirmed this DB-level patch does not survive a subsequent full zig build test-integration run -- some other test binary's own tenant-schema (re-)provisioning path re-triggers runForSchema() for tenant_default, which reapplies migration 035 (adp09_tamper_evident_audit_chain.sql, which defines the original UUID-typed bpm_audit_chain_canonical_payload/bpm_audit_compute_chain_hash) and then permanently skips GBL-082 again, silently reintroducing the exact defect. This confirms the bug is deterministic and code-level, not a one-off test-database corruption, and requires a code fix in src/db/migrations.zig -- out of scope for ISS-0093's own narrow helpers.zig shim-removal task, which does not touch migration dispatch logic.

While diagnosing ISS-0184/GH-517's 93 test-integration-svc failures, found that audit_entries.resource_id is now correctly TEXT on the live schema (this issue's original defect is resolved), but at least 6 test files still query it as `resource_id = $N::uuid`, producing C42883 'operator does not exist: text = uuid'. Reproduced directly: `SET search_path TO tenant_default,public; PREPARE q(text) AS SELECT status FROM instance_projections WHERE instance_id = $1; EXECUTE q(...)` style reproduction against resource_id confirmed the exact error text via psql. This is the inverse of the original ISS-0094 defect (call sites never updated after the column type changed, rather than the column type never changing) and accounts for the largest single cluster (C1) in the ISS-0184 diagnosis -- roughly 18+ raw occurrences in the postgres server log across ext02_webhook_dispatch_test.zig, obs03_audit_log_test.zig, obs05_dlq_test.zig, adp02_tenant_scope_test.zig, adp06_pipeline_run_correlation_test.zig, and oidc09_jit_provisioning_test.zig, with further cascading transaction-abort failures in xc02/xc06/exp201_202/exp401_402/exp601/repository_test/sim01_04 downstream of the first hit in each test's transaction. Fix is mechanical: remove the `::uuid` cast from the resource_id bind parameter in each affected query (or bind as text explicitly) across the ~6 files. Not fixed in this diagnosis pass (ISSUE-FIXER does diagnosis only); recorded here as this issue's continuation rather than a new issue number since it's the same resource_id/text/uuid story.

prevention: When adding a new GBL-prefixed migration, do not assume the 'GBL-' prefix alone is sufficient signal for 'this is public-schema-only' -- verify against the actual tables/functions the migration touches, and if it operates on any table that exists per-tenant-schema (audit_entries, process_definitions, instance_projections, tasks, dead_letter_items, webhook_subscriptions, webhook_deliveries, events, etc.), it must not be silently skipped for non-public schemas by filename-prefix alone.

A migration dispatch rule that infers scope from a naming convention (filename prefix) rather than from the migration's declared/actual content is inherently fragile -- prefer an explicit, machine-checked scope declaration per migration file over prefix-based inference.
